title: Sidónio Pais's coup
summary: Sidónio Pais, an officer and former minister who had been Portugal's envoy in Berlin, rose against the Democratic government on 5 December 1917 and took Lisbon after three days of fighting; Afonso Costa was arrested and President Bernardino Machado deposed and exiled. Pais governed as head of a junta and then, from April 1918, as a president elected by direct universal male suffrage — a form the 1911 constitution did not provide for — with parliament reduced and the parties pushed aside. He restored relations with the Church, courted Catholic and monarchist support, and kept Portugal in the war while withdrawing support from the expeditionary corps. The regime, called the New Republic, ended with his assassination a year later. It is in the atlas as the first successful military intervention of the republic and a precedent for those that followed.
